purpose: Investigate split-K and QMM scheduling to improve Q4 1K-token prefill on the M1 (jwm1-linux); paired alternating screen on both drivers with exact digests; qualify source only if repeatable and correct, otherwise receipt-only negative.
question: Does split-K scheduling or a small-n tile reroute of the Q4 prefill qmm path improve longctx-1024 prefill throughput without breaking pinned generated-id digests?

source.change: Two default-off scheduling screens behind env knobs, plus their kernels/tests/docs: MLX_OMARCHY_QMM_SMALLN_TILE=<n> routes matrix_n<=n qmm prefill dispatches to the register-blocked tile kernel; MLX_OMARCHY_QMM_SPLITK=<auto|2-8> splits the coopmat k-walk across CHUNK_K-aligned workgroup planes into f32 partials (shaders/qmm_coopmat_splitk.comp) reduced once (shaders/qmm_splitk_reduce.comp); auto targets ~512 threadgroups like native qmm_splitk. Profile ids appended after SdpaDecodeNativeF16 (QmmPrefillCoopmatSplitKF16, QmmSplitkReduceF16).
source.default_path_unchanged: With neither knob set the qmm dispatch takes the identical coopmat/tile route; the default arm reproduced all three canonical pins in every clean-window rotation.

hardware.host: jwm1-linux, Apple M1 (G13G B1), kernel 7.1.6-1-1-ARCH, AC power, /tmp/m1-gpu.lock held per window, bench_matrix clean-check + wheel RECORD vs loaded-lib gate on every leg

kernel_probe.summary: f16-scale quantized_matmul, m=1053: split-K auto splits only the concurrency-starved k/v shape (1053x896x128, 132 tiles -> s=4) and cuts it 0.811 -> 0.686 ms (-15.4%, dispatch delta 2 = split kernel + reduce) while leaving every full-grid shape untouched (delta 1, identical f16 digest). Tile reroute is 47.7% SLOWER than coopmat on that shape (1.198 ms). Forced split-8 regresses the big shapes catastrophically (1053x896x9728: 19.4 -> 30.4 ms).
kernel_probe.correction_record: An earlier probe pass (probe-f32scales-misconfigured/) used f32 scales, which promoted the whole call to QmmTileF32 and measured nothing relevant; kept as the method-error record. All conclusions above come from the corrected f16-scale probe.

paired_screen.protocol: Three arms on one exact release wheel (default / MLX_OMARCHY_QMM_SMALLN_TILE=128 / MLX_OMARCHY_QMM_SPLITK=auto), three rotations with rotated arm order (AB, BA, AB generalized), alternating under one lock window; every leg asserts bench_matrix clean-check, wheel RECORD match, and the canonical Q4 generated-id pins; arm-vs-pin failure on default retries (fragmentation guard), knob arms record-and-continue.

stock.knobs_inert: cooperative_matrix_f32_8=0 keeps both knob routes unreachable; all three arms pass the pins; tile128 and splitauto short medians are bit-identical (193.548), as expected for identical computations.

digest_findings.splitauto: DETERMINISTIC generated-id change: long-decode-128 -> f873dc2bdd34c0fe and longctx-1024-decode-32 -> 31267e7ed4c6d0dc on every attempt in every rotation; short unchanged. K-splitting reassociates the per-output f32 accumulation (contiguous CHUNK_K-aligned partials summed in ascending split order), so this is inherent to split-K, not a bug. The repo landing bar is digest equality, so split-K cannot qualify as source for these prompts.
digest_findings.tile128: Pins hold across all rotations: routing n<=128 to the tile kernel preserves generated ids (tile and coopmat kernels share the per-output accumulation order), although raw f16 outputs differ between the kernels (probe digests).
digest_findings.forced_split8: All shapes split; digests change on every workload.

tests.suite: omarchy_matmul_family_tests (20 cases), built on jwm1 from .work/mlx at 1323dc80
tests.fork_splitauto: 20/20 passed (tests-fork-splitauto.log); the scheduling-knob case additionally asserts the split route via dispatch deltas (2 for splitk+reduce on the starved shape, 1 elsewhere) and host-oracle bounds
tests.stock_default: 20/20 passed (tests-stock-default.log); knob modes are unreachable without cooperative matrix support (caps=0 keeps the knob code behind the coopmat gate) and the stock paired arms pass identical pins

fragmentation_hazard_found.observation: Under concurrent GPU load the DEFAULT arm itself flipped long-decode-128 to f873dc2bdd34c0fe twice (2026-09-10 ~15:04-15:15 window); on a quiet machine the pins reproduced in every later run, and CanonicalParity12's independent 12-rep canonical matrix on b6d662a8 never saw the flip.
fragmentation_hazard_found.mechanism: The qmm coopmat gate falls back to the tile kernel when lhs/output buffer element offsets are odd; allocator pressure under load changes sub-allocation offsets. The tile fallback is not digest-neutral, so heavy contention silently changes generated ids.
fragmentation_hazard_found.consequence: Digest gates must run on a quiet machine; a pin mismatch that vanishes on retry is environmental, not a regression. The bench_decode_identity wrapper (device_info() before model load) triggers the same class of flip and is not digest-safe as a harness engine. Worth a dedicated hardening ticket.

thermal_and_timing_procedure: All legs through scripts/bench_matrix.py (pinned model revision a5339a4131f135d0fdc6a5c8b5bbed2753bbe0f3, temp 0, seed 0, fixed warmup, clean-process check, no contended runs accepted, AC power). Paired medians over 3 order-rotated legs per arm per workload; prefill_tok_s is prompt-phase throughput for the exact recorded prompt token counts (30/262/1053).
rationale: Split-K (auto and forced): deterministic generated-id change on long and ctx1024 - fails the repo's digest-equality correctness bar - and its 1K prefill effect is nil (+0.11% median, kv shapes are too small a share of 1K qmm time).

Small-n tile reroute: digest-safe but regresses 1K prefill -3.2% (median paired), and the kernel probe shows the coopmat kernel is 47.7% faster than the tile kernel on the target shape at current main; the 2026-09-09 receipt's tile advantage does not reproduce on current code.
Nothing qualifies for landing; no source merges to main. The screens stay on this branch, default-off, as the reproducible instrument behind this receipt.
side_finding: Split-K lifts SHORT (30-token) prefill dramatically on the fork (333.3 -> 447.8 tok/s median, +34.3%, pins intact on short) because the k/v grids there are nearly empty (4 tiles). Out of scope here (assignment is 1K prefill) and recorded only with its caveat: the same knob breaks long/ctx1024 digests, so any future short-prefill use needs a digest-preserving split policy (e.g., splitting only shapes whose partial sums provably round identically), which does not exist today.

next.lever: For 1K prefill the remaining gap to native is not qmm scheduling: the qmm kernels are issue/barrier-bound per receipts 2026-09-09-prefill-qmm, the starved k/v shapes are worth only ~6 ms of ~946 ms, and both scheduling screens here are negative or digest-breaking. Cross-eager-scope dispatch fusion (fewer FastRope/RmsNorm/elementwise dispatches) remains the recorded next lever from receipts/2026-09-10-decode-bound-3.
next.hardening: File the contention-driven tile-fallback digest flip (and the bench_decode_identity wrapper hazard) as a known fragility of digest-gated benchmarking; quiet-machine requirement is currently implicit.
